title: Two-rank sparse fixed-path cohesive force and portable restart
purpose: Prove that disconnected split-interface traces can be coupled through an interface-scaled owner schedule without duplicated force or rank-local state identity, and that the accepted Explicit state can change MPI rank count.
physics: Two-dimensional normal and mixed-mode bilinear cohesive interfaces in finite-strain assembly and Explicit dynamics

execution.evidence: Three interface facets are recovered from declared cell partitions, cross two disconnected bulk partitions, exchange sparse trace/force payloads, and write a partial transient on two ranks that continues on one rank.

observables: Global equal-and-opposite interface force and exact integrated positive-side resultant.
Global cohesive stored energy and one physical owner per facet.
Node-wise agreement with the serial kernel for nonuniform compression, elastic opening, and softening.
Communication metadata bounded by required remote interface nodes, rank workload balance, and PETSc event names for constitutive, vector, and matrix work.
Identical structured Explicit energy history on every rank.
One-rank restarted displacement and irreversible maximum-opening state relative to an uninterrupted reference.
Mixed-mode normal/shear resultant and all physical-facet state fields on two ranks.
acceptance: The total cohesive force is zero to 1e-12 absolute and the positive-side resultant equals strength times reference interface length.
The global stored energy equals the exact elastic triangular area at peak opening.
Every physical facet appears exactly once in the distributed snapshot.
Every distributed interface-node force and both cohesive energy channels match the serial nonuniform reference to 1e-13.
Per-rank trace and force payload counts equal dimension times the scheduled remote interface-node count.

The collective performance profile reports the same global facet and payload counts on every rank; wall-clock evidence is obtained from the declared PETSc log events rather than a noisy CI time threshold.
The sparse schedule and node-wise serial equivalence pass with both two and three facet-owner ranks.
Two-rank-to-one-rank continuation matches displacement and cohesive history to 1e-11 relative.
limitations: Sparse payloads use communicator-wide Alltoallv; extreme-scale neighbor-graph performance is not yet a validated result.
The benchmark covers blocked P1 displacement and two-node 2D facets; the separate vector-interface benchmark owns material-law detail.
It does not validate the JMPS/Science crack-speed observations or a full thin-three-dimensional crack.
